Subject: Post-demo: proposed 4-week validation sprint + ownership (AstraGrid)

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciated the time and the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation I pulled together a short, pragmatic validation sprint we think will surface the effort, risks, and early metrics you asked for. Attached is a one-page plan plus a sample data schema. High level:

- Duration: 4 weeks (kickoff week + 3 evaluation weeks)
- Objective: validate Redwood’s inference quality and cost/growth model for AstraGrid’s internal ticket summarization and SLA routing flows
- Success criteria (pass/fail thresholds):
  - Summary ROUGE-L >= 0.45 on the seeded test set (Priya, we used the sample you shared)
  - End-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for median ticket size (<= 1,000 tokens) under a 5 qps sustained load
  - Token cost per ticket <= $0.015 at batch sizes aligned to your workload

Proposed owners:
- AstraGrid: Tom (stakeholder/acceptance), Priya (technical lead, dataset & eval), SRE/infra contact TBD
- Redwood: Karthik (engagement lead), Marissa (sales engineer & eval runs), Hannah (program sponsor)

Next steps we recommend (in order):
1) Confirm acceptance criteria above (reply with any tweaks)
2) Sign the attached one-page engagement (covers data access, trial scope, and minimal security terms) — e-sign or reply-all with approval
3) Schedule a 60-min kickoff next week to finalize dataset access and run cadence (we can use the Hudson room in the Drive link)

I attached the sprint plan and the sample schema we used to sanity-check the numbers today. If this looks good I'd like to lock dates and get the kickoff on calendar.

Thanks —
Hannah

Hannah —

Thanks for the concise plan. Priya and I reviewed it and we like the structure. Two quick clarifications before we sign:

1) The ROUGE-L threshold — can you confirm whether that is computed on normalized text (we remove boilerplate)? Priya says the sample she sent has a fair amount of template language.
2) The latency target — is the 300ms measured from Redwood API entrypoint to last token emitted (not including our internal proxy)? We need to compare apples-to-apples with our in-house latency numbers.

Also, we will need a short statement on data handling for the legal team (just 2–3 lines) — specifically: ephemeral caching, no retention beyond the trial by default, and KMS usage for payloads in transit if possible. Can you provide that in the kickoff?

Assuming those are okay, we can sign the one-pager by end of day Friday and schedule kickoff for next Tuesday.

Best —
Tom

Tom / Priya —

Thanks — quick answers inline below, plus a proposed kickoff agenda and a draft e-mail we can send to your legal team.

1) ROUGE-L: yes — we compute on normalized text by default. We run a small normalization pipeline that strips common templates and headers. If you prefer, Priya can send a short sample pre-processing script we used for the attached CSV.

2) Latency: the 300ms number is measured from our public API to last-token-emitted on our side (so excludes your proxy). If you'd like a full-path measurement we can run the test with your proxy in the loop during the second week.

Data handling stub for legal (draft):
"Redwood will process trial payloads in transit using TLS and optional customer-managed KMS. Trial request payloads are not persisted beyond the duration of the trial by default; ephemeral caches (used for performance) are disabled unless mutually agreed and will be cleared at trial end. Redwood will provide audit logs for trial activity upon request."

Proposed kickoff agenda (60 min):
- 00–10m: introductions & confirmation of owners
- 10–25m: data access & schema mapping (Priya + Redwood SRE)
- 25–40m: evaluation plan & metrics (ROUGE-L calc, sampling rules)
- 40–50m: test harness & run cadence (how we'll execute weekly runs)
- 50–60m: legal checklist & next steps (signing + data transfer method)

I attached a one-page runbook + the e-sign link once you confirm. Karthik & Vivek will join the kickoff to own infra/setup.

If that works, Hannah — please add the kickoff to the calendar for Tuesday, Jul 9, 11:00–12:00 PDT.

Cheers,
Marissa
